model_annotation:
The first plot, labeled "(a) 1B Models," illustrates the inference time across various batch sizes for three distinct models. The x-axis is labeled "Batch size" and features a discrete categorical scale presenting the values 1, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, and 300. The y-axis is labeled "Inference time (seconds)" and utilizes a linear scale with tick marks at intervals of 2 units, ranging from 0 to 10. The data is represented by grouped colored bars rather than lines. The blue bars, corresponding to the "Llama-1B" model, start at approximately 3 seconds at a batch size of 1 and exhibit a steep upward trend, reaching a peak of roughly 10.5 seconds at a batch size of 300. The orange bars, representing "Llamba-1B," start near 1.5 seconds at a batch size of 1 and gradually increase to about 4 seconds at a batch size of 300. The red bars, representing "MambaInLlama-1B," begin near 1 second and slowly increase to approximately 3 seconds at the final batch size of 300, accompanied by floating text labels above the bars such as "x3.6" at the start and "x3.7" at the end of the x-axis.

The second plot, labeled "(b) 3B Models," illustrates the inference time across various batch sizes for three different models. The x-axis is labeled "Batch size" and uses a discrete categorical scale displaying the values 1, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, and 512. The y-axis is labeled "Inference time (seconds)" on a linear scale that ranges from 0 to 30, with tick labels placed at intervals of 10 units. The data is again displayed as grouped bars. The blue bars for "Llama-3B" start at approximately 6 seconds at a batch size of 1 and show a sharp increase to nearly 30 seconds at a batch size of 256; at a batch size of 512, the blue bar is absent and marked with the text "OOM". The orange bars for "Llamba-4B" start at roughly 3 seconds and steadily ascend to approximately 13 seconds at a batch size of 512. The red bars for "MambaInLlama-3B" begin near 2.5 seconds and rise to about 11.5 seconds at a batch size of 512, with text labels floating above the bars indicating multipliers that range from "x2.6" at a batch size of 1 to "x4.2" at a batch size of 256.
